correctness.rationale: For every integer m≥1, two-agent binary utility vectors imply that any (1,1) allocation is EF+PO and any (1,0)/(0,1) allocation is PO when (1,1) is absent. A subset on which nonidentical valuations disagree yields an envy-free extreme allocation. For identical valuations, a nonzero complementary-11 pair yields EF+PO; if no such pair, all Pareto-efficient allocations have one agent at utility 0 who envies the utility-1 bundle. For plain EF the complementary equality criterion is exact. Each complementary pair gives three admissible identical function patterns, minus allzero, yielding 3^L-1; no EF permits only two patterns, yielding 2^L; 16^L is the exactly counted independent-fair sample space. An independently implemented exhaustive definition-level checker passed all 65,808 profiles for m=1,2,3; finite testing is explicitly not substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: Recent work identifies empty-set normalization as a central parameter in arbitrary Boolean division but gives only coarse classwise guarantees. The exact two-agent iff identifies the actual global obstruction: coincidence of entire valuation tables plus absence of complementary valued bundles. The result shows that even within both endpoint normalization classes every pair of differing valuations is feasible, locates the difference between EF nonexistence and EF/PO incompatibility, and supplies a natural exact probability under the uniform finite Boolean benchmark. This is a complete classification with a motivated substantive distinction, not merely a renamed allocation or a generic integer sequence. Limits to two agents and the artificial independent truth-table prior are explicit.
